OK, I have commented on the diff about nits and a few non-trivial issues. In addition, something needs to happen when one calls `pause()`. One could reject all the pending play promises with `AbortError` in `pause()`, but I don't think that's quite good enough. If one has called `play()`, it could be that the media pipeline has already begun to play but we don't know about it yet. A `play()`+`pause()` sequence could thus cause `currentTime` to progress a little bit, and it would be very strange if the play promise was rejected even though a tiny bit of playback happened.

I see two alternatives:
1. Treat `play()` and `pause()` as async commands that will be handled in order, so that a long sequence of alternating play and pause calls will normally result in a long sequence of successfully resolved promises, and tiny jumps in `currentTime`.
2. Like above, but with short-circuiting added, so that on the process where media playback happens, one will honor only the last requested state. This means that the `play()` promises will either all be resolved or all rejected.

These questions are tightly connected with https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/309 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/310

The question of alternating `play()` and `pause()` calls is a lot like alternating `activate()` and `deactivate()` with `MediaSession`, which @doomdavve implemented as each request being tracked on its own. If we could do that for `HTMLMediaElement` I think that'd be nice, but there may be other constraints implementation-wise.

Regarding the `play()`/`pause()` issue, @foolip and I discussed on IRC and decided that as long as it properly resolves in the case of the element is ready to play, it is fine. I think this new version handles it.

(The promised top-level comment.) The current spec is a little bit broken, in that there aren't any events fired once we are _actually playing_ or _actually paused_, the `playing` and `timeupdate`+`pause` events that are fired are speculative and can come before `currentTime` has begun or stopped moving, respectively. This is https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/309 and https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/310.

As mentioned in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/509#issuecomment-173203696 there are different ways one could handle multiple pending `play()` and `pause()` calls. To expand on option 1, which I prefer, each `play()` or `pause()` call would return a unique promise, and each promise is tied to an async request to the media pipeline. Each of these promises should be settled in order, just as they would be if they were spaced seconds apart. This will handle the situation where `play();pause()` is called on a paused media element, where `currentTime` actually progresses slightly. It should also cause a long series of alternating calls to result in the same number of actual plays and pauses in the media pipeline. (Batching of requests to "optimize" such a situation still couldn't fix the `play();pause()` problem.)

With this model in mind, resolving or rejecting the pending play promises as a group is problematic. I haven't yet figured out precisely how to spec it, but I think making the concept of a "media player" with which one communicates with message passing would force the solution into roughly the right shape.

Thoughts? Not everything should be fixed in this PR, and none of the above is set in stone. It would be nice to move closer to the goal though.

> (Batching of requests to "optimize" such a situation still couldn't fix the play();pause() problem.)

You could "await a stable state" to play or pause, where only the last call is honored. "When a media element is removed from a Document" already does so before pausing, per spec.

Yes, but whatever point we pick for batching up calls, it'll be possible to have two calls on each side of that point, and for the first of the calls to not be finished when the second one happens. At most I think this kind of approach could reduce stuttering caused by buggy scripts that call `play()` or `pause()` way to much.
Yeah. I don't have an opinion on which approach is best here.

I've just uploaded a commit applying your comments (the PR is getting bigger so I will rebase before merging, it might be easier for you to review).

Regarding the top level comment, my understanding is that how it is spec'd, this is what will happen:
- `play()` is called and we start fetching data; then `pause()` is called before the data is available. Then the promise from `play()` is rejected with `AbortError`.
- `play()` is called while data is available (ie. step 7.4). In that case, we will queue a task to resolve the promise. If `pause()` is called just after, it will queue a task to reject the promise. However, the resolving task will be run first so the promise will be resolved.

I believe this is a good enough behaviour in the context of this change. WDYT?

I realized something. In the current spec, you can actually keep using a media element after a network or decode error, and already buffered and decodable time ranges can be played. Although the `error` attribute is never cleared it also doesn't prevent playback from happening. In fact, it looks like if one calls `play()` while `readyState` is `HAVE_CURRENT_DATA`, and get a network error, then after seeking back to a buffered range can cause the `playing` event to be fired. The new steps in `play()` prevent a script from to play after any kind of error.

So, in the cases where it's still possible that a `playing` event will ever be fired, I think we need to leave the promise unsettled until it's either fired, or it cannot ever be fired. Only errors that happen while `readyState` is less than `HAVE_FUTURE_DATA` and that make it impossible to ever reach `HAVE_FUTURE_DATA` are really unrecoverable.

Getting this right may require sorting out https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/346 and splitting errors into recoverable and fatal types, but please have a look at the situation before I dig further.

You are definitely right that we need to queue a task to process the list of pending play promises to get the right order in some cases. I've looked at all occurrences of "list of pending play promises" and it looks like all of the problematic cases are inside `play()`:
- The `NotAllowedError` rejection. To queue a task for this one seems pretty strange.
- When the `error` attribute is null. As discussed in the previous comment this may have to go.
- In step 8 where we're already playing, queue a task to get the same timing as for the final "otherwise" step of the `paused` branch above.

However, fixing this wouldn't address the whole issue in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/509#issuecomment-174466222. Even though `pause()` queues a task to reject pending promises with `AbortError`, queueing a task doesn't guarantee anything about what happens on other threads and processes, so it's still possible that the play has already begun in the media pipeline and that we'll learn about this soon by currentTime moving. However, in this situation the playing events would also go missing, as the `readyState` transition steps only fires it if `paused` is false.

So, if the promise is always resolved when the `playing` event is fired and never otherwise (rejected or unsettled) I think that this will stick close enough to the current web of lies that it's acceptable and a good first step. I really want to sort out this mess though :)

In "style, typos and refactoring (no normative changes)" is what it seems, most importantly I made steps for "resolve pending play promises", "reject pending play promises" and tweaked/renamed "notify playing steps" to "notify about playing".

In "Limit play promise rejection to cases that are hard failures," I've arguably made the feature less complete, by not handling all errors that we know can happen, excluding both network error, decode errors and user abort errors. Why?
- "Fatal network errors that occur after the user agent has established whether the current media resource is usable" could be anywhere on the timeline, i.e. not at `currentTime`, and they aren't really fatal. There currently is no event for "`currentTime` has stopped because data is unavailable due a network error." The play promise (and existing API clients) will be left hanging in this situation.
- "Fatal errors in decoding the media data that occur after the user agent has established whether the current media resource is usable" don't make total sense. Common media frameworks will simply skip over "small" errors, and a fatal corruption of the rest of the file must still leave the earlier parts of the media timeline seekable, like a network error. Presto didn't report this error once playing, and I have low confidence in the API for implementors and web developers.
- "The fetching process is aborted by the user, e.g. because the user pressed a 'stop' button" isn't a thing any longer. Not implemented in Chromium at least.

So, I removed cases that I think we would soon regret if we began to sort out these problems. I added a rejection in the media element load algorithm, which would take care of any promises left pending indefinitely.

Note also that per design, the media resource selection algorithm itself can be left waiting for `source` child elements, in which case pending play promises will also be left hanging until the media resource selection algorithm continues.

Please review :) I can file issues to sort out the error handling messes once we're done with this.
